title: SiMOA pT73-Rab10 Homebrew Assay
author: yuan.yuan
materials: This protocol describes how to prepare biotinylated detector antibodies (IgG). The NHS‐PEG4‐biotin used in this protocol is an amine‐reactive ester that couples to primary amine groups (-NH 2 ) of proteins. The hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG) spacer improves water solubility. Other reactive groups (carboxyl, –SH) and spacers can be tried, but some optimization will be needed. This guide specifies preparing and testing an initial lot of detector with 1 mg/mL of antibody and a 40:1 ratio of biotin to antibody. Each biotinylation reaction requires 130 μg of antibody and will produce approximately 50 to 80 μg of detector. Detector antibody for Homebrew pT73-Rab10 Assay is Recombinant Anti-RAB10 antibody [MJF-R23] Abcam Catalog #ab237703 Workflow for Preparing Detector Antibody
Workflow for performing Simoa Assay on SR-X

steps.title: Buffer Exchange Capture Antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare the capture antibody (Recombinant Anti-RAB10 phospho T73 [MJF-R21], Abcam #ab231707) by exchanging its buffer into Bead Conjugation Buffer (BCB). Keep BCB and Bead Wash Buffer on ice.

substeps.instruction: Block Amicon filter: Add 500 uL of 1 mg/mL IgG (diluted from 2 mg/mL stock with 1X PBS) to the filter and centrifuge at 17,000 x g for 1 minute at room temperature; remove flow-through.
Determine stock antibody concentration using BCA assay and A280.
Calculate antibody mass for a 150-uL reaction with 30% excess (e.g., 0.04 mg for 0.2 mg/mL coating concentration).
Remove storage buffer: Add calculated antibody and BCB to a total volume of 500 uL in a 1.7 mL tube, vortex, spin down, and transfer to a pre-blocked Amicon filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature; collect flow-through in a separate tube.

Perform buffer exchange: Add 450 uL BCB to the filter, centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature. Collect the first wash ('Wash 1') for efficiency testing; discard subsequent washes. Repeat up to 3 times if filter volume exceeds 50 uL.

steps.title: Recover and Dilute Capture Antibody
steps.instruction: Recover the buffer-exchanged antibody and adjust it to the final reaction concentration.

substeps.instruction: Invert filter into a clean Amicon tube and centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature to transfer antibody to a tube labeled 'Buffer Exchanged Antibody'.
Wash filter membranes by adding 50 uL BCB, pipetting multiple times, and centrifuging at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes to transfer rinsate to the antibody tube.
Estimate volume using a P-100 pipette (expected 70-100 uL).

Measure concentration via BCA assay and calculate the volume of buffer-exchanged antibody and ice-cold BCB needed for a 150 uL total batch volume based on the target coating concentration (0.2 mg/mL).
Mix calculated antibody and BCB in a 1.7-mL tube, vortex, and confirm final concentration via spectrophotometer at OD 280 (blanked with BCB). Keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare and Wash Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Prepare Paramagnetic Carboxylated Beads and wash them prior to activation.

substeps.instruction: Determine stock bead concentration via Certificate of Analysis and calculate volume needed to provide 1.4 x 10^9 beads/mL for the batch volume (e.g., for 150 uL batch, if stock is 1.22x10^9/mL, use 172.13 uL).
Vortex beads for 30 seconds and rotate at 100 rpm for at least 10 minutes at room temperature; transfer calculated volume to a 1.7 mL tube.
Wash beads 3x with Bead Wash Buffer: Use a magnetic separator (1 min), aspirate supernatant, add 150 uL Bead Wash Buffer, vortex 5s, pulse spin, and repeat.
Wash beads 2x with cold BCB: Use a magnetic separator (1 min), aspirate supernatant, add 150 uL cold BCB, vortex 5s, pulse spin, and repeat.

steps.title: Activate Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Activate the carboxylated beads using EDC. Timing is critical; use ice-cold buffers and avoid idle time.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 mg/mL EDC: Add 1 mL ice-cold BCB to a 10-mg vial of EDC and vortex until dissolved.
Calculate EDC volume for 0.3 mg/mL final concentration (e.g., 4.5 uL for 150 uL batch).
Resuspend beads in cold BCB (Batch Volume minus EDC volume, e.g., 145.5 uL), vortex, pulse spin, and place on ice.

Activate: Vortex beads (~30s), immediately add calculated 10 mg/mL EDC stock, vortex for 10 seconds, and rotate for 30 minutes at 2-8 °C. Protect 488 Dyed-beads from light using Parafilm and aluminum foil.

steps.title: Conjugate Antibody to Beads
steps.instruction: Couple the capture antibody to the activated beads.

substeps.instruction: Wash activated beads: Centrifuge 1-2s, place in magnetic separator (1 min), aspirate supernatant, add 150 uL ice-cold BCB, vortex 5s, centrifuge 1-2s, place in magnetic separator (1 min), and aspirate supernatant completely.
Conjugate: Add 150 uL ice-cold buffer-exchanged capture antibody to beads, vortex 10s, and rotate for 2 hours at 2-8 °C. Ensure homogenous mixing.

steps.title: Wash and Block Conjugated Beads
steps.instruction: Clean the beads and block remaining active sites.

substeps.instruction: Collect reaction supernatant: Centrifuge, place in magnetic separator (1 min), and transfer supernatant to a tube labeled 'Supernatant'.
Wash beads 2x with Bead Wash Buffer: Add 150 uL buffer, vortex 5s, centrifuge, place in magnetic separator (1 min), and transfer first wash to 'Wash 1' tube; discard second wash.
Block beads: Add 150 uL Bead Blocking Buffer, vortex 5s, centrifuge, and rotate for 45 minutes at room temperature. Protect 488 Dyed-beads from light.
Final Wash: Centrifuge, place in magnetic separator (1 min), aspirate, add 150 uL Bead Wash Buffer, vortex 5s, centrifuge, place in magnetic separator (1 min), and aspirate.
Resuspend: Add 150 uL Bead Diluent, vortex 5s, centrifuge, place in magnetic separator (1 min), aspirate, then add a final 150 uL Bead Diluent. Mix, centrifuge, and store at 2-8 °C.

steps.title: Determine Antibody Coating Efficiency
steps.instruction: Quantify the amount of antibody successfully coupled to the beads.

substeps.instruction: Measure antibody concentration in 'Supernatant' (blank with BCB) and 'Wash 1' (blank with Bead Wash Buffer) using a spectrophotometer at OD 280.
Calculate the amount of antibody coated onto the beads.

steps.title: Prepare and Biotinylate Detector Antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare the detector antibody and conjugate it to NHS-PEG4-Biotin.

substeps.instruction: Buffer Exchange: Block Amicon filter (as in step 1.1). Determine stock Ab concentration (BCA/A280). Calculate mass for 100-uL reaction with 30% excess (e.g., 0.13 mg).
Remove storage buffer: Add calculated Ab and Biotinylation Reaction Buffer to a total of 500 uL in the filter; centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes. Discard flow-through.
Wash: Perform 2-3 buffer exchanges with 450 uL Biotinylation Reaction Buffer at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes each.
Recover: Invert filter into a tube, centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes. Wash membranes with 50 uL Biotinylation Reaction Buffer and centrifuge again at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes.
Adjust Concentration: Measure concentration (OD 280, blanked with Biotinylation Reaction Buffer) and add buffer to reach 1 mg/mL. Confirm final concentration is 0.95–1.05 mg/mL.

Biotinylation: Reconstitute NHS-PEG4-Biotin (warm to RT) with 383 uL deionized water to 8.9 mM. Mix 1 mg/mL antibody, reconstituted biotin, and Biotinylation Reaction Buffer (suggested 40x ratio), vortex, centrifuge 2s, and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Purify Biotinylated Antibody
steps.instruction: Remove unbound biotin from the detector antibody.

substeps.instruction: Concentrate: Add conjugated antibody to a blocked Amicon filter, add Biotinylation Reaction Buffer to 500 uL total, and centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes. Discard flow-through.
Wash: Perform 4 washes with 450 uL Biotinylation Reaction Buffer at 14,000 x g for 5 minutes each.

Recover: Invert filter into a tube, centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes. Wash membranes with 50 uL Biotinylation Reaction Buffer and centrifuge again at 1,000 x g for 2 minutes. Final volume should be ~90 uL. Store at 4 °C.
Characterize: Measure concentration (OD 280, blanked with Biotinylation Reaction Buffer) and calculate reaction yield.

steps.title: Prepare Standards and Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the calibration curve and experimental samples.

substeps.instruction: Standards: Use HEK-293T protein lysates (R1441G-LRRK2/Rab10) to create a dilution series (1000 pg/mL to 0.1 pg/mL) using Homebrew Sample Diluent Buffer. Use diluent for 0 pg/mL. Transfer 100 uL per well.

Samples: Quick thaw samples at 37 °C and immediately place on ice. Dilute serum/plasma 10-fold (10 uL sample + 90 uL diluent) or urine exosomes 3-5 fold (e.g., 20 uL sample + 80 uL diluent). Transfer appropriate volume of diluent to wells, add well-mixed sample (e.g., 5 uL sample + 95 uL diluent), and mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Run Simoa Assay
steps.instruction: Perform the 2-step Simoa assay on the microplate shaker, washer, and SR-X instrument.

substeps.instruction: Incubation: Incubate samples, calibrators, and bead solution with detector solution at RT on microplate shaker at 800 rpm for 1 hour. Cover with lid or foil.
RGP Preparation: Solubilize RGP by heating with vigorous shaking at 800 rpm (e.g., 1 °C for 120 min, 25 °C for 60 min, 30 °C for 30 min, or 35 °C for 20 min).

Washing and SBG: Transfer plate to Simoa Washer. After the first wash, incubate with 100 uL SBG for 10 minutes at 37 °C at 800 rpm. Complete the 2-step wash protocol. If bead pellets are too high, manually add buffer B, shake, magnetize, and aspirate.
Analysis: Load tips, micro-discs, and RGP into Quanterix SR-X. Define plate layout and run the dry plate within one hour of washing.

steps.title: Review and Evaluate Results
steps.instruction: Export data from the SR-X and evaluate assay performance.

substeps.instruction: Export: Generate and export the run report (PDF/Excel) and run data (CSV) to an external drive via the SR-X home page.

Evaluate LOD/LLOQ: Check AEBs for standards. LOD is calculated at 2.5 x STD above Cal A Average AEB. LLOQ is the lowest concentration where CV < 20%. Signal-to-background (Cal A to Cal B) should be 2.5–3.
Check Assay Characteristics: Ensure background (fon) is < 0.02 AEB (ideal 0.005–0.01). Target signal should be ~16 AEB; avoid levels > 20 AEB to prevent optical saturation.
